title: Whole units, losses and converter loops

blocks.text: Conversions must not round a tiny offer up into free power. The long-valued bridges move exact representable quanta; a remainder stays in its original storage instead of being invented or silently claimed as transferred.
Illustrative arithmetic, not a server setting
rows: 5 J converts to 2 FE; a smaller offer can be insufficient.

blocks.text: Input and output losses are independent, but the bridge uses one base ratio. Very precise ratios can require a large quantum. If that quantum exceeds the transfer rate or remaining buffer space, transfer pauses. That is not necessarily a broken cable.

GT block packets are rounded conservatively at packet boundaries, rather than using a fictional simulated packet API. Fractional AE item operations also use conservative rounding. No simulation is supposed to debit storage.

A safe round trip inside Calculator does not prove an entire modpack is free of converter loops. Another mod can use a different exchange rate. Prefer inherit, align all converters, or deliberately close incompatible routes. Changing rates with charged buffers changes their native-equivalent value; it does not rewrite stored FE.
Power is connected but not moving
